lines.text: Twenty dots. How many squares can you make with them?
lines.caption: Twenty dots. How many squares can you make with them?

lines.text: Most kids find twenty. <short pause> But there are MORE hiding in here.
lines.caption: Most kids find twenty. But there are MORE hiding in here.

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's find every last one, together.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's find every last one, together.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: We have twenty dots, in four rows of five.
lines.caption: We have twenty dots, in four rows of five.

lines.text: Neighbouring dots are one unit apart.
lines.caption: Neighbouring dots are one unit apart.

lines.text: How many squares have all four corners on dots?
lines.caption: How many squares have all four corners on dots?

lines.text: And here's the twist: count squares of every size, including tilted ones.
lines.caption: And here's the twist: count squares of every size, including tilted ones.

lines.text: Is it twenty, twenty-four, twenty-six, thirty, or forty?
lines.caption: Is it twenty, twenty-four, twenty-six, thirty, or forty?

lines.text: So what are we really looking for?
lines.caption: So what are we really looking for?

lines.text: Pick any four dots. If they make a perfect square, it counts.
lines.caption: Pick any four dots. If they make a perfect square, it counts.

lines.text: Like this little one.
lines.caption: Like this little one.

lines.text: Squares can be bigger, like this one.
lines.caption: Squares can be bigger, like this one.

lines.text: And this one counts too, even though it's standing on its corner!
lines.caption: And this one counts too, even though it's standing on its corner!

lines.text: Our job is to count them ALL, without missing any, and without counting any twice.
lines.caption: Our job is to count them ALL, without missing any, and without counting any twice.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Our first strategy is to sort the squares by size.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Our first strategy is to sort the squares by size.

lines.text: Let's start with the upright ones. They sit straight, like floor tiles.
lines.caption: Let's start with the upright ones. They sit straight, like floor tiles.

lines.text: The smallest are one by one. The grid is four squares across, and three down.
lines.caption: The smallest are one by one. The grid is four squares across, and three down.

lines.text: So that's four times three. Twelve!
lines.caption: So that's four times three. Twelve!

lines.text: Next, two by two squares. Let's slide one around the grid.
lines.caption: Next, two by two squares. Let's slide one around the grid.

lines.text: It fits in three spots across, and two spots down. That's six.
lines.caption: It fits in three spots across, and two spots down. That's six.

lines.text: Three by three squares fit in just two spots.
lines.caption: Three by three squares fit in just two spots.

lines.text: Can we go bigger? A four by four square needs four units of height, but our grid is only three tall. So, no.
lines.caption: Can we go bigger? A four by four square needs four units of height, but our grid is only three tall. So, no.

lines.text: Twelve, plus six, plus two. That's twenty upright squares.
lines.caption: Twelve, plus six, plus two. That's twenty upright squares.

lines.text: Twenty! Are we done? <short pause> Not yet. Remember the tilted squares?
lines.caption: Twenty! Are we done? Not yet. Remember the tilted squares?

lines.text: Here's the smallest tilted square. Each side goes one across, and one down.
lines.caption: Here's the smallest tilted square. Each side goes one across, and one down.

lines.text: It fits snugly inside a two by two box.
lines.caption: It fits snugly inside a two by two box.

lines.text: We already found six two by two boxes. Each one holds one of these. So, six more!
lines.caption: We already found six two by two boxes. Each one holds one of these. So, six more!

lines.text: Now a bigger tilted square. Each side goes two across, and one down.
lines.caption: Now a bigger tilted square. Each side goes two across, and one down.

lines.text: It fits inside a three by three box. And look, it has a mirror twin!
lines.caption: It fits inside a three by three box. And look, it has a mirror twin!

lines.text: Two three by three boxes, with two tilted squares each. That's four more.
lines.caption: Two three by three boxes, with two tilted squares each. That's four more.

lines.text: Any bigger tilted square would need a four by four box. That doesn't fit.
lines.caption: Any bigger tilted square would need a four by four box. That doesn't fit.

lines.text: So we have twenty, plus six, plus four. <short pause> That's thirty squares!
lines.caption: So we have twenty, plus six, plus four. That's thirty squares!

lines.text: Now here's a faster way. I call it the box trick.
lines.caption: Now here's a faster way. I call it the box trick.

lines.text: Every square, upright or tilted, fits snugly inside an upright box. It touches all four sides.
lines.caption: Every square, upright or tilted, fits snugly inside an upright box. It touches all four sides.

lines.text: Look at this two by two box. It holds the box itself, plus one tilted square. That's two squares.
lines.caption: Look at this two by two box. It holds the box itself, plus one tilted square. That's two squares.

lines.text: Now a three by three box. The corners step along its sides, from dot to dot.
lines.caption: Now a three by three box. The corners step along its sides, from dot to dot.

lines.text: Zero steps. One step. Two steps. With three steps, we are back to the box! So, three squares in one box.
lines.caption: Zero steps. One step. Two steps. With three steps, we are back to the box! So, three squares in one box.

lines.text: See the pattern? A two by two box holds two snug squares. A three by three box holds three.
lines.caption: See the pattern? A two by two box holds two snug squares. A three by three box holds three.

lines.text: So we just count the boxes, and multiply by their size.
lines.caption: So we just count the boxes, and multiply by their size.

lines.text: Twelve one by one boxes, times one, is twelve.
lines.caption: Twelve one by one boxes, times one, is twelve.

lines.text: Six two by two boxes, times two, is twelve.
lines.caption: Six two by two boxes, times two, is twelve.

lines.text: Two three by three boxes, times three, is six.
lines.caption: Two three by three boxes, times three, is six.

lines.text: Twelve, plus twelve, plus six. Thirty again!
lines.caption: Twelve, plus twelve, plus six. Thirty again!

lines.text: When should you use the box trick? When the grid gets big. It saves a LOT of drawing.
lines.caption: When should you use the box trick? When the grid gets big. It saves a LOT of drawing.

lines.text: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
lines.caption: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: Twenty is what you get if you forget the tilted squares completely.
lines.caption: Twenty is what you get if you forget the tilted squares completely.

lines.text: Twenty-four means you missed the six small tilted squares.
lines.caption: Twenty-four means you missed the six small tilted squares.

lines.text: Twenty-six means you missed the four big tilted ones. And forty is just too many!
lines.caption: Twenty-six means you missed the four big tilted ones. And forty is just too many!

lines.text: So here's a great habit. Sort by size, and always ask: did I check for tilted ones?
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. Sort by size, and always ask: did I check for tilted ones?

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Here's a bigger grid.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Here's a bigger grid.

lines.text: Now there are twenty-five dots, in five rows of five.
lines.caption: Now there are twenty-five dots, in five rows of five.

lines.text: How many squares have all four corners on dots? Tilted ones count too.
lines.caption: How many squares have all four corners on dots? Tilted ones count too.

lines.text: Try the box trick!
lines.caption: Try the box trick!

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. This grid is four units across, and four down.
lines.caption: Let's check. This grid is four units across, and four down.

lines.text: One by one boxes: sixteen of them. Times one, that's sixteen.
lines.caption: One by one boxes: sixteen of them. Times one, that's sixteen.

lines.text: Two by two boxes: three across and three down, so nine. Times two, that's eighteen.
lines.caption: Two by two boxes: three across and three down, so nine. Times two, that's eighteen.

lines.text: Three by three boxes: four of them. Times three, that's twelve.
lines.caption: Three by three boxes: four of them. Times three, that's twelve.

lines.text: And one big four by four box. It hides four squares!
lines.caption: And one big four by four box. It hides four squares!

lines.text: Sixteen, plus eighteen, plus twelve, plus four. <short pause> That's fifty!
lines.caption: Sixteen, plus eighteen, plus twelve, plus four. That's fifty!

lines.text: If you got fifty, amazing work!
lines.caption: If you got fifty, amazing work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: Sort squares by the box they fit in snugly. A three by three box holds three snug squares.
lines.caption: Sort squares by the box they fit in snugly. A three by three box holds three snug squares.

lines.text: And never forget the tilted ones!
lines.caption: And never forget the tilted ones!

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep counting, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep counting, and I'll see you next time!
